chunks.text: The peepal or sacred fig (Ficus religiosa) is a species of fig in the family Moraceae, also called the bodhi tree or ashvattha tree, native to the Indian subcontinent, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Pakistan and parts of Indochina. It is a large, semi-evergreen to dry-season-deciduous tree reaching up to 30 metres tall with a trunk that can be 3 metres across, and is easily recognised by its heart-shaped leaves with a long, drawn-out drip tip. Its small figs, only 1-1.5 cm across, ripen from green to purple, and it is pollinated by a specialised fig wasp, Blastophaga quadriceps. The species can live for an extraordinarily long time — the Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi in Sri Lanka, grown from a cutting of the original Bodhi tree taken in 288 BCE, is over 2,250 years old and is considered the oldest human-planted flowering tree in the world with a known planting date.

chunks.source: Wikipedia — Ficus religiosa (religious and cultural significance)
chunks.text: The peepal holds deep religious significance in Buddhism, Hinduism, Jainism and Sikhism. Gautama Buddha is said to have attained enlightenment while meditating under a peepal tree at what is now Bodh Gaya, Bihar; not every peepal is considered a true 'Bodhi tree' — only those propagated in an unbroken lineage from that original tree qualify. In Hindu tradition the tree is called ashvattha in Sanskrit and is mentioned extensively in scripture including the Rig Veda; the Padma Purana links the peepal with Vishnu, the banyan with Shiva, and the plaksha fig with Brahma. Devotees traditionally circle the tree seven times in the morning while chanting a salutation to it as the 'king of trees.' Peepal-leaf motifs appear on seals and pottery from the Indus Valley Civilisation dating to the third millennium BCE, and India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna medal, is modelled on a peepal leaf. In parts of traditional medicine the tree has been used for a wide range of ailments including asthma, diabetes and gastric problems, though it is also classified as an invasive or weedy species in some non-native regions such as Hawaii.
